english_fact_card.what_happened: Developer Urban Splash has been ordered to pay more than £45.7m to the government after fire safety defects were repaired in seven high-rise buildings in Manchester. The buildings were developed between 2000 and 2008, and defects were discovered after the Grenfell Tower disaster. The remediation cost over £60m, with £51.1m from the Building Safety Fund. The tribunal ruled on Thursday that Urban Splash must contribute £45.7m.
english_fact_card.who_affected: Urban Splash, residents of the affected buildings, taxpayers
english_fact_card.why_now: The tribunal ruling is a new development in the fire safety remediation case.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Accountability for fire safety defects in Manchester high-rises.
english_fact_card.reader_action: No immediate action; follow any appeals.
